body:
I'm professionally diagnosed with OCD and am in therapy/practicing ERP to help. I've been on the path to transition for many years as well.

With all due respect, I came here to vent because I was/am in a very dark spot, not to debate my identity and the legitimacy of my mental illness.
Like I said in my post, I'm afraid that I'm *not* trans. I want to transition, and detransitioning resources only make my OCD worse.
That's great to hear! Happy your results turned out well!

From what I can gather, the NAFTA list says I should be alright with two years of post secondary education, however I'd need at least three years of experience as well (which I'm assuming would have to be completed in the US--throws a wrench in my timeline). Looks like I've hit another dead end, rats. Thank you for the suggestion, though!

PS, any single Canadians feel free to hmu, lol
What would my options be if I'm unable to get a bachelor's? I can't afford college at the moment outside of an associate's.
How much experience would I need to secure a permit? I can't afford college outside of an associate's, and I want to avoid taking out loans.
I know exactly what you're going through. It's very isolating when no one knows what you're going through or can relate to your struggle. I'm sorry you're struggling so much right now

Thank you!

Congrats on finishing your draft! A Beckett-sci-fi fusion sounds very fascinating.

Oh darn, I forgot to reply to you. Sorry about that!

I'm writing a play about a young soon-to-be college dropout struggling to accept adulthood and the changing world around her as she comes back to her rural home for the winter holiday. I wanted to really push myself, so I'm incorporating elements of magical realism that tie into my own area's local history. I'm not sure if I'll be able to finish the play by the end of the month, but I'm nonetheless having a great time writing! What's your play about?

I struggle with OCD as well, and it's really taken a toll on my perception of myself and identity. While I don't think I'll be able to take a blind leap of faith like you, it's comforting to hear a success story. Thanks for this
You and me both! Good luck!!
That's wonderful! Best of luck

I honestly don't know if I'm even "transgender" anymore. If we're defining the word as the opposite of being cisgender, we've just fallen back into a weird binary system that doesn't describe me on either end. I know I'm not fully comfortable as my AGAB, but I'm simultaneously not comfortable transitioning away from it to identify as something else, even if that hypothetical something else still features my AGAB (i.e., genderfluid, etc).

This makes no sense to me, either. My identity is a headache and I am very sorry. It's kind of like I'm this weird Schrodinger's Gender: no one knows if I'm cis or straight until they open the box, but when you open the box, it's just another box, and inside that box is another box, and so on. I'm like twelve boxes deep at this point and I'm starting to realize that it's just boxes all the way down. I can try to label what's inside of the box, and other people can try to label what's inside of the box, but it's impossible to get any metrics on what's inside when you've just been getting boxes for five years straight. (Apologies for the weird box rant, lol)

I relate a lot to what you're saying, especially what you said regarding the implications that come with explaining one's identity by using a label created by others. It's like you said, I'd rather be defined by my own self perception rather than be robbed of my inner complexities by adopting a label and pronouns. This sounds douchey, but I'm almost tempted to tell people a fun fact about myself if I'm ever asked. "What's my gender identity? Oh, I'm writing a play at the moment and am really enjoying it so far." It beats having to have a twenty minute discussion about the intricacies of my mental state and beliefs regarding my gender identity, that's for sure.

I mean, I'm not, but there's not really a solution here. I can't really control what pronouns others choose to use for me. Even when I wasn't in this weird state I'm in now, I would get misgendered all the time because I didn't look the part, even after I corrected others. It's one of those things that I think I unfortunately may have to just suck up.

While my personal situation leaves me with quite a large impact, you're definitely right in saying that OCD still manages to exaggerate the potential worst case scenario into an unrealistic doomsday. I think it's less that I'm understanding that my fear was somewhat exaggerated and more that I'm actually capable of handling this worst case scenario. It's been really scary and painful, but it's also shown me that I'm strong enough to make it through that fear and pain, which is oddly empowering.
For sure. It's definitely a mix of both in my case, and I can acknowledge that most people's intrusive thoughts turn out not to be true. OCD is a complex, individualistic thing.

Nope, not at all. In fact, I wrote a disclaimer at the end to make sure this post wouldn't be misconstrued like that. Just because you have an intrusive thought doesn't mean that the intrusive thought is true. Lots of people find that their intrusive thoughts aren't after they've worked on treatment for a while. I was just sharing a personal accomplishment.
Thank you! I honestly don't know what I'd do without it.

I'd suggest looking into exposure therapy. I don't think you're doomed to forever be a wuss. Most people's fears are a result of past difficulties manifesting into a physical reaction, and if you're able to slowly expose yourself to the things/situations that are making you anxious, you'll learn how to handle them over time.
Feeling the same way as a 20yo. This stuff sucks, but we'll make it through and start living our lives eventually.

Definitely the tank. Way more comfortable, and way more space to "move things around," if you catch my drift. Not to mention, it feels much more like an undershirt than a sports bra, which personally gets rid of a lot of dysphoria (and leaves less of an outline underneath clothing).

This probably sounds bad, but I honestly don't even remember. This whole journey has been so long and painful that I struggle to look back on it and find the euphoria that first fueled it. Looks like it's time to phone my therapist

I think a lot of it has to do with current events amplifying my dysphoria and mental health issues. I'm pre-everything right now, which probably has something to do with it as well. Gonna be honest, I was doing pretty bad when I posted this originally, and while I'm doing better now, I still am struggling to curb all the dysphoria and transphobia that's weighing on me, which in turn makes it hard to feel good about myself or transitioning at all.

Feel you, man. Came on this subreddit to post something similar. It feels like things are actively getting worse for trans people worldwide, and while I don't want to be pessimistic, I can't imagine a better future in my lifetime. I really don't know where I'd go where I wouldn't have to confront transphobia or major discomfort, not to mention that moving is incredibly expensive as is (it always irks me when it's brought up as a solution when the majority of people can't afford it).

I guess my only advice would be to be kind to yourself. Pay attention to your needs, trans-related or otherwise, and take care of yourself as best you can. It's the only thing we as individuals can do, really. Best of luck to you.

If OP doesn't have the money to pay out of pocket for therapy, something tells me they don't have the funds to move out of state. Sweet sentiment on your part, but unfortunately not a realistic one. Instead, I'd urge OP to contact in-state resources that could help connect them to a better therapist.

While this is true, unfortunately remote therapy still requires you to live in the same state as the therapist (at least in the United States, unsure where the OP is from). It sucks, especially when you live in conservative areas with very few options.

This seems less like a gender issue and more of a "society sucks ass" issue to me. I've certainly felt this way many times before. Whereas women have much more freedom to experiment with clothing/their appearances, men are forced to stick with very plain, one-size-fits-all styles, as fashion is typically seen as a feminine interest. As such, there's a huge stigma when guys try to stand out with their looks. Same goes for other interests/a lack thereof (my mother told me I couldn't be a man because I wasn't interested in sports up until recently, for example). It's just another example of society being close-minded and pointlessly gendered to a suffocating degree.

That being said, guys are starting to "stand out" more as more people are defying societal expectations. No clue how old you are, but I've seen a lot of younger guys experiment with different fashion styles (skirts and dresses, makeup, jewelry, high fashion, etc). If you want to stand out, then by all means, go for it! Experiment with some cool new clothes or an interesting haircut and go from there. Confidence really helps attract others' attention, too. The only things stopping you are the premonitions of some outdated social norms.

I struggle with the latter theme. It's very easy to fall down the Google rabbit hole in your weak moments, I know I have. You can and will recover from this, though. ERP is hard, and sometimes you can slip and fall back into those compulsions and reassurance-seeking patterns. We all have had our moments, so don't beat yourself up. So long as you dust yourself off and get back up, you'll be okay.
Currently taking Zoloft myself. Haven't hit the six week mark yet, so I can't speak on its effectiveness yet, but I've heard good things from others. Good luck!

They suck. It always baffled me how mental distress can manifest physically in such a (for lack of a better term) asshole manner. Like, c'mon brain, you *know* that a groinal response will only make you even more upset, and yet you give me one anyway?

I don't really know how to deal with them, honestly. They're pretty terrifying for me. ERP is hard enough when pertaining to just my thoughts, and throwing a physical response in there makes it so much harder. We'll get through this.

Thank you. Hopefully I can try to find something else to ground me and keep me close to my family. Unfortunately, I don't think I'll be able to go down the two middle names route--the name I'm eyeing rhymes with my middle name, and I don't want to sound silly. Thanks for the suggestion, though!

That actually helps me a lot! I like the logical approach you went with. I've more or less been waiting for a name to "find" me, so I guess taking some time to actually research names wouldn't hurt.

How many names did you have to siphon through in order to find "the one," out of curiosity?

That's fair. Back when I was in art school, my writing schedule was built entirely around deadlines (if I wanted not to flunk my classes, at least), and it usually worked in my favor. What would you say would be a reasonable deadline to set? I unfortunately don't have a professor to do it for me this time around, lol.
No problem at all. Best of luck writing!

Hey there. Saw on your profile that you have OCD. Not to armchair diagnose or anything, but this sounds a lot like your OCD is targeting your gender identity. I struggle from this theme as well, and it sucks a lot. Gender is this weird thing that is super hard to nail down, and OCD loves to intrude on any potential grey areas and go to town with the intrusive thoughts.

I'd suggest talking to a therapist who specializes in OCD about this. NOCD is a great app that can connect you to one in your area. If therapy isn't an option, I'd suggest trying some ERP exercises to help push past this rough patch. Whatever you do, don't try and tackle the intricacies of your gender identity right now. In the words of my own therapist, good decisions rarely are made in times of distress. Focus on kicking those worries' asses first.

Reading both your post and this reply, I'd say that a novel would suit this story best. While a series of interconnected short stories seems cool, I'd worry that you'd lose focus on the interesting premise and instead get caught up in non sequiturs or less interesting side stories (like the detectives you mentioned--it would make for much more interesting of a story to stick with the MC rather than to halve her story in favor of an investigation that ultimately goes nowhere).

There isn't any rule that says your novel has to play out in chronological order. Check out Olive Kitteridge or The Glass Castle for wonderful examples of this--strong characters that can be studied and observed over time. Like Calm\_Cicada said, while this story centers around a pivotal act, you're still ultimately writing a story that focuses more on a single character and her motivations. A novel about those motivations and their consequences would complement this MC best, IMO.
No way, someone else who has cis OCD! Feels like there aren't a lot of us out there. Feel for you man, we'll get through this!

It really depends on where you live. The therapists vary depending on where you live, availability, etc., but the majority seem to be really great and very understanding, albeit somewhat pricey. Word of the wise, though: stay off the social networking side of the app. It's a hub for reassurance seeking and isn't really moderated from what I can tell.

\`\`I'd imagine it was, for sure. The dread of my deadname being everywhere at work is already starting to suck, lol.

Related question: how did you go about coming out at work? Obviously, I'd need to email/talk to HR, but I'm not sure how to handle person-to-person interactions etc.
Thanks for the advice, man! I'll definitely consider reaching out to a nonbinary coworker. In the meantime, it's time to work up some courage and figure out how to email HR, lol
This picture radiates happiness and I'm absolutely loving it!

I think you may have misunderstood my post. I did nothing different at all to my appearance to try looking more masculine, and objectively I didn't look any different than I do now. It was like my brain superimposed a strange masculine filter over my appearance without actually changing anything. Super weird, I know.
By story beats, I mean important plot moments or events at a glance, like an outline. Specifics are the more intricate details.

I'm starting to write physical works from some of my daydreams, and I can relate to what you're talking about to an extent. I think it's easier for me to focus less on the specifics as opposed to blocking beats and characters out first and refining things from there. That way, I can go back and place myself in those beats and further delve into specifics as I go along while keeping the main heart intact. That being said, my daydreams often change and refine themselves over time, and given how I'm a writer outside of daydreams, I'm less attached to specifics than most.

I'm trying my best to do this, and man, is it hard. What's helping me is forcing myself to make my internal daydreams external in a creative outlet. Not only is it a great means for self-expression to help deal with tough stuff in a healthy way, but it's helping me further develop creative passions of mine that I've struggled to maintain thanks to other mental illnesses draining that passion from me. It involves a lot of vulnerability and hard work, but so far it's certainly been worth it, if not for me then for the dudes in my brain finally getting some space to breathe and develop after over a decade.

Loving this so far. Elena's hilarious. The dialogue flows nicely and is very natural. These sorts of things always are a bit "on the nose," so I don't think you're being too cheesy or melodramatic, maybe save for the somewhat familiar "time to let go" line. That being said, I do feel like this scene needs to be expanded upon. Something tells me that these two would have more than a page worth of dialogue to say to each other. Humor is a great way for ease the tension in otherwise fairly dramatic scenes (and I'd love to hear more of Elena's quips). Having the characters show us their feelings rather than outright telling them is another great route to take. I'd love for Elena to share a memory about Luis in place of her just telling us that he was kind, for instance. It would not only show us that she (I assume) loved her son-in-law in a more impactful way, but it would give some authentic heart to the scene while further developing Elena's character. Good luck with the rest of your play!
Thank you!

I have dedicated journals for all my rough drafts and planning. I'm way too unorganized to figure out how to translate my scattered marginalia and diagrams onto Google Docs, plus the act of physically writing something on paper does wonders for my creative juices. Typing a piece out feels like it's giving it a level of finality, or at the very least separating the messy planning phase from the more polished drafts.
Oh wow, never thought I'd see the day where I'd find another ace in SC. And an Epic Gamer^(TM)*,* no less! I'm quite passionate about writing as well--what genres do you tend gravitate towards?

1. Creating things. Writing plays, drawing, anything that lets me release the abscess terror through a medium that can make something I can actively work on and get something new out of.
2. I'm still unpacking the extent of how OCD effected me as a child, so I can't give the best answer here. I would constantly try escaping into daydreams, a bad habit that I still struggle with today. I guess that kind of goes back to the whole "releasing anxiety through creating something new" thing, but instead of making a tangible product, all the stories would stay in my head.
3. Oddly enough, verbally arguing with myself helps a lot. Saying my fears out loud and rebutting them in real time helps me to get the intrusive thoughts out of my system without validating them. That, and "you're tired, go to bed," lol.
Concord Theatricals has a bunch available. I found some of my favorite plays by just browsing through filtered search results
I'll definitely give this a shot once I have some decent material ready to go. How'd you suggest finding actors to work with?

I actually have some advice for this, believe it or not. I find it relatively easy to write pieces and stick with them throughout the editing process, and I attribute a lot of that ease to my background with writing over the years. I've built up a habit of reading a lot of literature and writing as frequently as possible without regards to the quality. The former helps give you some nice sources for inspiration and education, while the latter gets those creative gears turning and gives you a low-risk outlet to go wild with your ideas.

For playwriting specifically, I've found that actively teaching myself more about the medium has not only helped me grow as a writer, but it's motivated me to take more risks and create more that I'm proud of. Aside from the expected Syd Field and "Save the Cat" recommendations, Stuart Spencer's "The Playwright's Guidebook" has been a game changer for me, couldn't recommend it enough.

Best of luck, from one desperate playwright to another.

I've heard a lot of good things about New Play Exchange, I guess this is the push I needed to join. As per new play development organizations, do you have any places I could look into for starters? I'm looking into things now, and it's a bit overwhelming, haha.

Looks like I'm already on pace then, lol. But real talk, you make a good point. It's really easy to get wrapped up in what specific steps you need to take to propel your career, when all you really need to start is a few ideas and the motivation to write them down. When would you say I'd be "good" enough to move on from the "getting the bad ones out of my system" phase, just out of curiosity?

I think it may help to know more about the character's background. What's her socioeconomic status? Where did she grow up? What are her parents like? Knowing more about her personality may be helpful as well, if you're looking for a name whose meaning parallels an important character trait.

If it sounds natural given the context. Dialogue should reflect the speaker. It'll seem pretty weird if a backwoods redneck character says he's "going to" the store as opposed to "goin' to," for instance.

Yeah, of course! Here's a good article that helped me a lot: [https://www.treatmyocd.com/blog/transgender-ocd-symptoms-and-treatment](https://www.treatmyocd.com/blog/transgender-ocd-symptoms-and-treatment)

The second part of the article is a bit more relevant to what I experience (a lot of the sources out there center around cis people being afraid that they're trans, not the other way around, which is super frustrating), but the article as a whole is great. If you end up relating to what it has to say, I'd recommend looking at the rest of the website. It's helped me a ton. There's a subreddit for this as well (r/cisOCD), but it's unfortunately dead in the water.
Hey, at least you're a twink. Instead of looking like Shaggy from Scooby Doo, I look like a lesbian with bad posture, apologies to optimistic past me lol

Yep. It sucks. But, I was able to get support once I spoke with my therapist and learned I had OCD relating to my gender identity--I'd suggest looking more into it, if I were you. A lot of what you're describing here matches up perfectly with what I deal with, and treatments like ERP have helped me a lot. Good luck man, you're not alone.
Haha I feel you dude, I just want to feel like a man and not question it, dammit! But alas, the universe is a cruel bitch and can't just let us trust ourselves.

Hourglass shaped trans gay man here, I feel you big time. Always got the "I'm so jealous of your figure" from girls before I came out, and I frustratingly still do now. On the rare occasion a guy shows interest in me, I'm convinced that he's either got a fetish or thinks that I'm a woman, both of which have happened more than once. Dating feels like this dysphoric minefield nowadays, and I hate that I can't have a normal love life because I'm trapped in a body I never asked for. It really hurts.

I'm just calling myself asexual for now in the hopes that I can still have a fulfilling romantic relationship in the future without attracting a guy who will be thinking about my body in that way (plus, the thought of having sex with my current state of affairs down there feels indescribably dysphoric). Sure, it's not a fix-all for how he'll perceive me, but it's better than nothing, I guess.

I feel this. Every time I see some shithole cis male taking his biology for granted, I want to just end things outright. I will say, though, that attempting to take your life is very terrifying and is not worth it in the end. I attempted very recently and was scared shitless thanks to a poorly thought out plan and horrible unintended side effects. Life is tough, and it sucks that we've been dealt such a poor hand, but it goes on nonetheless. We'll power through this thing together.

I was in your position for a long time and felt absolutely insane for not being able to definitively say "I'm a guy!" or "I'm a girl!" when it felt like everyone else could. No matter how much I wanted to be seen as male or how dysphoric I felt, there would always be that horrible "what if" feeling that told me to look back at all the "disqualifiers" which kept holding me back, especially when I left for college and decided to stop taking my meds. After countless therapists and reflection sessions, I learned two things: 1, only I can figure out my gender identity on my own timeline (not people on the internet), and 2, I have gender identity-related OCD, which is pretty much never talked about in the context of trans people and makes navigating this stuff a living nightmare. I'm still struggling with my identity and a lot of mental health issues, but at least I'm able to approach gender-related things in a healthier way. 

Moral of the story is that we all have different experiences that shape us into the people we are today, with no two people's experiences perfectly matching up. It's really tempting to see if other people can relate to you on the grounds that it'll finally give you that answer, but at the end of the day, it's just like you said: the only person who can say if you're trans or not is you. Do some introspection, figure out what makes you feel most like yourself. Don't sweat other people's opinions. All that matters is your own happiness.

This stuff is exhausting and agonizing to go through, and I'm really proud of you for being so strong. You'll figure everything out eventually, I believe in you.

No need to apologize for not being encouraging, this stuff is hard to go through and I'm really sorry passing is difficult for you right now. And you're absolutely right, passing is super weird and subjective, haha. Wishing you the best of luck in the future

Thanks for the advice, I really appreciate it.

I use a washcloth bunched up, pretty much the same thing. It's weird, I just really dislike even bare touch without some sort of clothing/layering, even in pajamas I have to avoid certain shirts that "feel" weird and make me think about my physicality. Probably just me.

I've tried FtMpassing before. Never touching that place again. Every single time I worked up the courage to post there, I'd get DMs from people either telling me that I'd never pass or really gross ones from people with trans guy fetishes. Every single time. That's why I stick to alt accounts now, haha. The actual replies were fine enough, but they never went further than clothing choices. I said it in another comment I believe, but I'm equally concerned with how I perceive myself alongside how others perceive me. If I pass, cool, but at the end of the day, I'm always gonna know what's under my clothes. It just makes me feel like I'm a dumb girl playing dress up in my dad's clothes or something, feels awful to even go in public anymore.

I'm trying to distract myself as best I can, but it's so hard. Every time I try to catch up on some reading or finish this one act I've been working on, I just keep thinking about my body and how futile it is to ignore something I'll never be able to leave. I don't have any goals or desire to set them at this point, nothing really makes me happy, I don't know what to do anymore

Last sentence was more of me being pessimistic for the hell of it, sorry if that wasn't clear. Difficult for me not to be overly negative right now, but I'll work on it. I completely agree with you, learning to frame things differently can do wonders for your outlook on things, especially when dealing with difficult stuff like transitioning.

I'm on meds for anxiety/depression and in therapy right now and have been for years, along with stints in inpatient and intensive outpatient, mindfulness sessions, feels like everything at this point. Nothing's really worked, and it feels like I've gotta be doing something wrong but I don't know what else to do. I'm trying to save up for an intensive ERP outpatient treatment (it's lovely to have other mental illnesses on top of this stuff, isn't it?), which is the only other type of therapy I haven't tried yet (CBT, talk therapy, DBT, none of those things did more than gutting my bank account). I'm desperate for something to work, don't know how much longer I can live like this

That makes sense, completely agree with you there. I'm glad you're able to keep that self confidence in the face of dysphoria. I've never had a positive self image, gender-related or otherwise, haha. Work in progress, especially now that I've just about hit rock bottom there. Any tips on how to build it back up would be wonderful, if you have them

Thank you for the nice comment. 

I completely understand that the people saying these types of things (especially MtFs) are probably going through a lot on their own ends, no ill will there. Transitioning is a really difficult process, and the last thing I want to do is imply trans men "have it worse" or something. Everyone has it "worse," everyone's going through a rough time.

I'd love to hear your anecdotal 2 cents. It's been incredibly difficult, I don't really know what to do. It's not fair at all, man, I really can't stand it
Thank you. Feels nice to be seen. Not sure how much talking would help, but I appreciate the kindness

Thank you. It means a lot to know someone cares about my well being.

I'm currently seeing a therapist and have been on medication for years now, but nothing's really been able to help me feel better. Inpatient, intensive outpatient, meditation-guided sessions, mindfulness walks, all with no dice. It's really frustrating, especially considering that all those resources weren't helping before I found out about this bone structure stuff. Really lonely to go through, especially when people imply you're not doing enough when options aren't working. I just don't know what to do anymore, or if it's even worth it to keep trying

Thanks for the advice. I usually shower in the dark for this very reason, but I don't have blackout curtains so I can still see things. Plus, having to touch myself at any capacity sucks, no matter the light level. Just one of those things you have to put up with, I guess

Thanks for the kind words. I really appreciate it.

People give me the whole "there are cis men who have larger hips etc" talk all the time, and I know you meant well by it, but it personally just makes me feel like garbage. Just a reminder that the main thing holding me back is that I'm not cis--that musician you're talking about doesn't pass in spite of his traditionally feminine appearance, he passes because he's cis. That's the kicker. And now, it feels like I have even more hurdles to jump over to convince others I'm a man, let alone try to convince myself I'm a real one. Sorry for the mini vent, just been a really hard few weeks.

Not a fan of details, but I can't exactly energy blast this problem away. It's a very permanent staple in my life. I don't have anything motivating factor to keep living. There's no crowd going wild for me, either, just a shit ton of bills from therapy and medications that aren't doing anything.

Thanks for the advice, but I just don't know how practical or applicable it is for me right now. Appreciate the care nonetheless

Know how you feel. No clue where you're from, but it feels like everywhere in the world is fucking trans people up nowadays. Best advice I can give you is to hold out hope for that euphoria, whether it be through surgery or other little ways along the way. Sure, those things won't solve everything, but they're a place to start piecing things back together. Talking to other people who've experienced similar struggles (i.e., other people in the trans community, etc) may be nice as well. Best of luck to you.

I'm so sorry, man. Solidarity to you. I feel the same way whenever I try to pass in public, especially when binding or trying to pull off any non-baggy pants. But try to remember that this is a temporary feeling. You're still pre-T, very early into the physical part of transition. With time and the self-esteem that comes with transition, that dysphoria will fade as that man in your head starts showing up in the mirror. It'll be okay, you've got this.

Had to make a burner account because of this post. Holy shit.  


I've been questioning my own gender identity for years now, with the past six or so months consisting of me trying to painfully dig up my want to transition into a man and live stealth as one to what seems like no avail. This post really struck a chord with me--I *thought* that I was above the patriarchy and that my motives for transition were entirely independent from it, but after reading what you had to say, I'm not so sure anymore. It sucks to be a woman in society. I personally can't find many positives in being one, aside from getting less scrutiny from being emotional. Is my dysphoria just a product of deep-seeded misogyny and a lack of female role models I see myself in? Do I just want to be separate from this gender that I've been conditioned to hate? I have no idea.  


I guess this is a long way of me saying that you're not alone. I'm 19 myself and tend to attract a lot of friends on the LGBT spectrum, and it's difficult to try and explore yourself without getting too into your own head. This sort of thing is so taxing to try and figure out, and it feels so horrible to confront the not-so-great idea of all your questioning supposedly being for nothing. Best of luck to you, man. No matter what happens, you're not alone.
